subject: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 latency regressions & TPS drop after quant/kern rollout
messages:
From: Jordan Price <ops-lead@finexa.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-ml.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 spikes and dramatic TPS drop (prod tokens/s)

Hi Laura —

Over the last 45 minutes our production traffic against the hosted endpoint serving model:redwood-v3-qa has seen p95 jump from ~120ms to ~520ms and p99 to ~1.2s. More worrying: measured tokens-per-second on steady-state payloads dropped ~3x (we use the token-per-second probe you suggested). Error rate on 200/stream responses is up ~2.8%.

This coincides with what looks like an infra push last night (your side) that mentioned quantization kernel updates. Can you confirm if any quantization profile or kernel selection changes were rolled? This is impacting a live payment flow for Finexa. We need immediate remediation or rollback.

Attached: small sample of our probe results (we'll upload more if helpful).

—Jordan
Ops Lead, Finexa Health

From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 spikes and dramatic TPS drop (prod tokens/s)

Thanks Jordan — got the probe sample. Initial triage notes:

- Confirmed a delta in tokens/s on our synthetic probes that mirrors Finexa's curves (3x drop during peak).
- Error spike primarily 502/503 transient errors tied to backend workers timing out waiting on KV-cache warms.
- Top hypothesis: the kernel selector started preferring a new quantized kernel variant for certain attention shapes; that kernel has suboptimal throughput vs previous path for the 1–2k token context we both use. The selector decision changed after a recent rule that weights quantized kernel latency estimates more heavily.

I'm attaching an anonymized perf dump and the minimal trace that maps to the time window you reported.

Attachments: perf_dump_0304.jsonl (sample), heap_trace_2026-03-05.txt (partial)

Next steps (short):
1) Marcus to validate rollout metadata & canary scope.
2) If selector is the culprit, plan a targeted rollback of the selector rule for model:redwood-v3-qa and force the previous kernel variant for the affected shapes.
3) If rollback is high-risk, consider a temporary routing policy to send Finexa traffic to a stable cluster (isolated) while we fix the selector logic.

I'll stay on the thread and assist with logs.

—Priyom
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Price <ops-lead@finexa.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 spikes and dramatic TPS drop (prod tokens/s)

Update from infra side after night investigation:

- Confirmed a canary/config push at 2026-03-03T23:40:22Z that adjusted kernel-selection weights for quantized kernels (change id: kc-20260303-77). The change was intended to reduce median latency for short-context traffic but the selector misclassified some longer-context batches (1k+ tokens) and routed them to a quantized kernel path that performs worse for these shapes.
- Reproduced locally: for a 1.5k-token iter, previous kernel = 450 tokens/s, new kernel = 150 tokens/s on same node type (A100-p4). This matches the ~3x drop Finexa reported.
- Root cause: a heuristic regressed due to an incorrect fallback threshold and a missing guard that should have kept the old kernel for >512-token batches.

Attached: kernel-change-log.patch, kv-cache-heatmap-0305.png and a short snippet of the selector config.

Mitigation executed 2026-03-05T08:05Z: rolled back kernel-selection rule kc-20260303-77 for model:redwood-v3-qa. We also applied a temporary routing override for Finexa's org-id to route to the stable cluster. Early telemetry shows tokens/sec returning to baseline within 18 minutes post-rollback. p95 reduced from ~520ms to ~140ms; p99 back to ~320ms in initial samples.

Next actions:
- Full postmortem + permanent selector fix (Priyom + Runtime) by EOD.
- QA regression harness to include longer-context quantized kernel benchmarks.
- Exec update going to be prepared for customer-facing summary.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Short update and apology: we identified the cause as a kernel-selection/quantization routing change that mistakenly routed longer-context requests to a quantized kernel with lower throughput. Marcus rolled back the selector rule and applied a short-term routing override for your traffic; you should see normal throughput and latency restored.

What we did: rollback of kc-20260303-77 + routing override to stable cluster (completed 08:05Z).
Immediate impact: tokens/sec and p95/p99 metrics returned to baseline within ~20 minutes.

Planned next steps:
- Full postmortem with timeline and mitigation plan (ETA: EOD today).
- Patch to selector logic + additional unit/integration tests for quantized-kernel selection.
- Option: scheduled maintenance window if you prefer us to run the permanent fix with you on a staged rollout.

We've escalated to Exec (Evelyn Hart) to ensure we sync on credits/contract implications and to coordinate the final customer-facing summary. Evelyn — appreciate any guidance on credits or SLA remediation we should offer.

Again, very sorry for the impact. Happy to hop on a call if you prefer a real-time walk-through.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
